title: Core registers
description: The shared registers every management system standard builds on, in five domains: Management system, Risk and controls, Operations, Privacy and security, and Suppliers. Standards are added as add-ons that extend these registers with their own columns, categories and views, so a risk, an incident or a document is recorded once and counts for every standard that uses it. Documents, risks and nonconformities come with approval workflows, and each record can link to the requirements of any framework you adopt.

levels.name: Foundations
levels.description: Where every management system starts: its context and scope, documents and policies, objectives and KPIs, and the risk register with its risk categories.

levels.name: Starter
levels.description: Everything in Foundations plus incidents, nonconformities and CAPA, actions and suppliers: the registers most standards use first.

levels.name: Full
levels.description: Everything in Starter plus the legal register, competence and training, internal audits, management reviews, the controls library and assets.

sheets.name: Risk register
sheets.description: Every risk and opportunity in one register. Each risk has a category, and each category has its own likelihood and impact scales and its own appetite (Risk categories). The score is likelihood times impact, before and after treatment (the residual risk). The risk owner, then top management, accept a risk through the Risk acceptance workflow.

fields.description: The category decides the scales and the appetite this risk is scored against.

fields.name: Likelihood
fields.description: On the category’s likelihood scale.

fields.name: Impact
fields.description: On the category’s impact scale.

fields.name: Appetite
fields.description: The highest score the category accepts without treatment.

config.expr: IF({score} = 0, "", IF(EMPTY({appetite}), "No appetite set", IF({score} > {appetite}, "Above appetite", "Within appetite")))

values.likelihood_scale: 1 Rare: not expected in the next five years. 2 Unlikely: could happen once in five years. 3 Possible: about once a year. 4 Likely: several times a year. 5 Almost certain: monthly or more often.
values.impact_scale: 1 Negligible: no lasting effect. 2 Minor: dealt with in a day. 3 Moderate: a week of disruption or a customer complaint. 4 Major: lost business, a regulator’s interest or harm to people. 5 Severe: the organisation’s future is at stake.

sheets.name: Nonconformities and CAPA
sheets.description: One loop for every nonconformity, whatever the standard: what was found, containment, root cause, the corrective actions and the check that they worked. A nonconformity closes only with a root cause and a verified effect, through the CAPA closure workflow: someone other than the owner checks that the actions worked.

automations.name: Context entry agreed → next review in a year
automations.description: Recurring review cycle: when an issue, an interested party or the scope is agreed, its next review is set a year ahead, so the 30-day reminder comes round again and changes reach the management review.

automations.name: Document approved → record the date and plan the next review
automations.description: Recurring review cycle: when the Document approval workflow approves a document, today's date is recorded as Approved on and the next review set a year ahead, so the review reminder comes round without anyone having to remember.

automations.name: Risk accepted → next review in a year
automations.description: Recurring review cycle: when top management accepts a risk through the Risk acceptance workflow, its next review is set a year ahead, so an accepted risk is looked at again before it is forgotten.

automations.name: High-severity incident → tell the investigator and top management
automations.description: Escalation: an incident marked High, by the person reporting it or later, reaches the investigator and everyone with the job title Top management at once, so a serious event is never left in the queue.

actions.message: {id} {name} is marked High. Look at it today.

automations.name: Action 14 days overdue → tell top management
automations.description: Escalation ladder: the owner is told the day after the due date; when an action is still open 14 days later, the owner and everyone with the job title Top management are told, so nothing stalls unseen.

actions.message: {id} {name} was due on {due} and is still not done.

automations.name: Supplier review in 30 days → tell the owner
Supplier approved → next review in a year
automations.description: Recurring review cycle: when a supplier is marked Approved, its next review is set a year ahead, so every supplier you rely on is looked at again.
